summary: Backend testing for the newly added Transactions sort options and Export/Import backup endpoints in HENZA DIGITECH. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_sort_backup.py with 16 tests: 7 sort tests (default, date_desc, date_asc, amount_desc, amount_asc, category_asc, unknown-key fallback), 2 export tests (shape/contract + _id exclusion across all 6 collections), 3 import merge tests (idempotent round-trip, delete-then-merge restores, replace-mode wipe+restore), and 4 malformed-input tests. All 16 new tests PASS. Full suite (16 new + 35 pre-existing) = 51/51 PASS. IMPORTANT: found and fixed a critical regression introduced together with the new /export /import endpoints — the /api/bills/upcoming decorator was accidentally concatenated onto the previous comment line (line 423 of server.py: `# ============ UPCOMING BILLS ============@api_router.get('/bills/upcoming')`), so the route was silently disabled and returned 405. Fixed by inserting a newline. Note: pytest.ini enables pytest-xdist with LoadScopeScheduling; the new round-trip tests mutate the shared MongoDB and MUST be run serially (`-o addopts=''`). This is how the test runner was invoked for reporting.

minor.issue: REGRESSION (now fixed by tester): the @api_router.get('/bills/upcoming') decorator was concatenated to the '# ============ UPCOMING BILLS ============' comment on the same line (server.py:423), causing Python to treat the decorator as a comment. Route was returning 405 Method Not Allowed. Inserted newline; route now registered and all upcoming-bills tests pass. Please review other decorators in the file for the same copy/paste pattern.

ImportBundle declares `transactions: List[dict]` (and similarly for other collections), so pydantic validation rejects non-dict items with 422 before prep() runs. The defensive `if not isinstance(it, dict): continue` inside prep() at server.py:668 is therefore unreachable. Not a bug — server does not crash — but the defensive code is dead. Consider using `List[Any]` if you want prep() to silently drop bad items instead of returning 422 to the client.

In merge mode, duplicates are detected only by exact `id` match. Documents that logically duplicate but have different ids (e.g. same transaction imported from two sources) will be inserted again. Acceptable for phone-migration scenario but worth documenting to users.

Import loops one document at a time (find_one + insert_one). For a large bundle (thousands of transactions) this will be slow; consider bulk_write with UpdateOne(upsert=True) for merge and insert_many for replace.

Files collection embeds base64 blobs and is exported inline by default (include_files=True). A user with many attachments may hit large response sizes / memory pressure. Consider streaming or an option to export files metadata + separate per-file download.

action_items: Review server.py for any other accidentally-joined decorator+comment lines (same pattern that broke /api/bills/upcoming). Consider adding a lint rule / pre-commit hook to detect '# ...@api_router' on a single line.
(Optional) Switch ImportBundle field types to `List[Any]` so prep()'s isinstance guard becomes reachable and malformed items are silently skipped instead of the whole request being rejected with 422.
(Optional) Use pymongo bulk_write for the import loop; per-item insertion will not scale for large migrations.

(Optional) Add an idempotency check that also matches on (type, date, amount, description) for transactions to reduce accidental duplicates when the user re-imports a partial bundle from a different device.
critical_code_review_comments: Regression risk: the /export and /import commit visibly disrupted the /bills/upcoming route by collapsing its section header onto the decorator. Same-line comment+decorator concatenation is easy to miss in review — good candidate for a lint/CI check.

sort_map in list_transactions correctly whitelists sort keys (safe against injection) and falls back to date_desc for unknown values. category_asc uses a compound sort with a secondary date_desc — verified by test.

Export excludes MongoDB _id via projection ({'_id': 0}) on every collection — verified. Bundle includes app='HENZA_DIGITECH', version=1, exported_at, counts (matches list lengths), and all 6 collections.
Import merge/replace semantics verified: merge skips by id, replace wipes then inserts. Round-trip is truly idempotent when nothing changed between export and re-import.
Files collection is exported in full including base64 `data` field (include_files=True default). This is correct for backup but see minor issue above about payload size.
seed_data_creation: test_sort_backup.py seeds 5 deterministic transactions (dates 2025-06-01..2025-06-21, mix of income/expense/categories, amounts spanning 10k..9M) tagged with 'TEST_SORTBAK_<uuid>' via a module-scoped fixture, and cleans them up at teardown. It also creates and cleans up two temporary items during the malformed-input test. Between test-file cleanup and pre-existing backend_test.py's own TAG-based teardown, the DB is left in its original state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully green. The new test file (test_sort_backup.py) mutates the DB across the whole app-wide dataset (export/import round-trip), so it MUST be run serially. pytest.ini in /app/backend enables pytest-xdist (`-n auto --dist loadscope`) which caused 3 spurious failures on the first run because TestImportReplace (mode='replace') on gw1 wiped the DB while TestImportMerge tests on gw0 were mid-round-trip. Run with `-o addopts=''` (or `PYTEST_ADDOPTS=''`) to disable xdist for this file. Sort tests are safe under xdist (they filter by q=TAG). Base URL is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env.
rca_of_issue: One real bug was found and fixed by the tester: `# ============ UPCOMING BILLS ============@api_router.get('/bills/upcoming')` at server.py:423 — decorator was on the same line as the section comment so Python treated the entire line as a comment; the /api/bills/upcoming function existed but was never registered as a FastAPI route, returning 405. Root cause: manual edit when appending the new /export /import sections stripped the newline between the previous section's end and the /bills/upcoming section header. Reproduction: GET https://.../api/bills/upcoming?days=7 -> 405 Method Not Allowed. Mitigation: restore newline before the decorator (done). After fix + backend restart, all 51 tests pass. Recommend adding a simple grep-based CI check: `grep -nE '#.*@(api_router|app)\.'` to catch this pattern.
